note.question: Can a high-quality firm distinguish itself through social-media spending and price when SMM both expands awareness and reveals more third-party quality information, and what spending patterns survive equilibrium refinement?
note.overview: The paper studies a two-period signaling game in which a privately informed firm chooses price and social-media-marketing expenditure, consumers update beliefs from those actions and a noisy quality signal, and equilibrium is characterized as a perfect Bayesian equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Period 1: the firm observes its true quality type and chooses SMM expenditure s and product price p. Period 2: aware consumers receive an external quality signal, observe s and p, update their posterior beliefs about quality, and buy exactly when expected quality is at least the price. The paper solves the sequential signaling game by backward induction. SMM is costly but expands the pool of aware consumers, so high expenditure is not a purely wasteful quality signal.
